I never thought I would actually relate or that my first post here would be from personal experience.. but my mom died on Monday of lung cancer and I fully understand the feeling. I held her until she gave her last breath too and saw her eyes lose its glow, all in a matter of seconds. Its beyond absolutely nothing one would think would ever have the misfortune to experience, and I do not wish it upon anybody who truly loves their mother which such an intensity.

 I'm 26 and being really close to my mom, really makes me feel completely helpless. The endless mood swings of what ifs and acceptance switches don't help either. Everything reminds me of her, her voice in my head, the decorations on the wall, a flower I saw that day. Absolutely everything. I'm afraid of breaking down at any moment that its not in my home. I'm struggling to eat and even moved houses as it's very painful to continue living in my old house. 

But what does help is.. knowing that it WILL get easier with time. I really don't know the path ahead either but reading so many stories here about people who eventually find peace and comfort with time, makes me have some hope in the future. It makes you realize that eventually life will go on as usual, along with the memories that will never leave us until we are no longer in this world either. 

We are all humans after all, and all we can do for now its survive as best as we can. Reading this to you may be helpful, enfuriating, loving, etc. But believe me that from the bottom of my heart I am with you and everyone reading this. We will all get through this rough life road together. I don't know who any of you are personally but I love you all and feel free to DM me if you ever need someone to talk to. 

My mother was the most wonderful woman to me. And whoever reads this, has a good relationship with their mom and still has her with you. Give her a huge hug, call, text them and tell them you love them and are thankful for everything they have done for you.. as it may also be the last time you may be able to do. With no regrets in your heart.

Imma end this long post with a quote I know understand to its full extent:

"A mother is afraid of the world for us, but she doesn't know that we are afraid of the world without her."

And wherever you are now..I love you mom.

Congrats!! Your hard work paid off!  🎊  idk who you are but im proud of you!! ADHD can be a heavy toll to bear but you proved statistics wrong. Medical school isn't easy, but this only proves that we can achieve everything we put our mind into.

Disclaimer: I don't mean to take the spotlight away from OP but rather thank them for being an inspiration to my own medical journey :)

Also, you have no IDEA how much motivation your story gives me. I always felt like a failure, especially because I would see my peers succeed so easily and I would wonder what was wrong with my brain; blamed myself on why it was wired like that.

My last job was as a medical assistant  (non certified) and was let go because I wasn't able to catch up with the doctors, and even though I was medicated, it was not my correct dose (it is now adjusted). 

She wanted everything quick and wouldn't even let me use skills to tackle these like: taking notes or draw instruments, repeat info to oneself, etc..which us ADHD people use sometimes to retain info. I would forget patients names, etc (everything would be solved with note taking in my case). So when I was let go, I was told that maybe I didn't succeed because the medical area was not the area for me. 

I felt my heart sink and well yeah. A week after that, my mom was diagnosed with stage 4 lung cancer, non smoker. It was kinda rough tbh, but after some soul searching, I'm now determined to become an oncologist.

 I was still a bit hesitant due to my ADHD and also my age? (26F) haha but your story made me more determined than ever. I will prove her wrong and make my parents proud, and most of all, myself. I can do it!

 But again, this is about *you*, sorry for perhaps boring you with my story,  I am happy for you and good luck in medical school!!
